payload.stem: In grasses, the guard cells of a stoma are:
payload.explanation: Grass guard cells are dumb-bell shaped, unlike the bean-shaped guard cells of most other plants.

payload.stem: Which wall of a guard cell is highly thickened?
options: The outer wall, away from the pore
The wall shared with the subsidiary cell
The inner wall, towards the stomatal pore
payload.explanation: The inner walls facing the stomatal pore are thick, the outer walls are thin, which helps the pore open and close.

payload.stem: Vascular bundles that have cambium between xylem and phloem are called:
payload.explanation: Cambium lets the bundle form secondary xylem and phloem, so such bundles are open.

payload.stem: A radial arrangement of xylem and phloem, on different radii, is found in:
payload.explanation: In roots xylem and phloem alternate along different radii. Stems and leaves usually have conjoint bundles.

payload.stem: Casparian strips on endodermal cells are made of:
payload.explanation: Water-impermeable, waxy suberin is deposited on the radial and tangential walls of endodermal cells.

payload.stem: A ring-like arrangement of vascular bundles is characteristic of:
payload.explanation: A ring of conjoint, open bundles is a hallmark of the dicot stem; monocot bundles are scattered.

payload.stem: When bulliform cells lose water and become flaccid, the grass leaf:
payload.explanation: Flaccid bulliform cells make the leaf curl inwards, which reduces water loss.
